text:
henry: headsup - saw p50 > p95 for /v1/embeddings at 09:17 UTC for one minute. screenshot attached, feels impossible.

leah: that can't be right unless we're mis-displaying percentiles. which aggregation are you looking at? histogram or t-digest?

henry: the card says "histogram rollup". toggling to raw samples shows normal numbers.

siobhan: ah this smells like interpolation noise from histogram buckets. we switched interpolation mode to 'linear' for UI smoothing last month. with coarse bucket boundaries you can get anomalies where the estimated median lands above an extreme percentile if counts are skewed.

jamal: quick reproduce: minute had samples ~= [95,110,120,125,480,495,510] (n=7). histogram buckets used were [0-200,200-600] -> counts 4/3. linear interpolation inside the second bucket for p99 pushed p99 estimate into the bucket centroid logic and p50 estimate got biased upward if interpolation used bucket edges incorrectly.

leah: so bug class: histogram aggregation + linear interp + small-n + coarse buckets -> inverted percentiles. UX fix: surface "aggregation source" (histogram/tdigest/raw) and interpolation mode in the card, and show an "exact" fallback button when n<50.

henry: +1. also add a safety check: if displayed p50 > p95 or p95 > p99 flag as "suspicious aggregation" with a hoverable explain.

console-bot: created CON-9999 "Latency percentiles: show aggregation provenance + interpolation mode + exact fallback for small-n histogram artifacts" assigned to eng-platform backlog.

siobhan: I'll run a small sim matrix to recommend default bucket width and when to prefer t-digest/raw. propose: if bucket_width > 200ms and n<100 prefer raw.

jamal: I'll wire a UI note and add a telemetry event when users hit exact fallback so we can tune perf.

henry: thanks all. tagging @siobhan @jamal @leah. closing until we have sim numbers.
